report:
Reviewed the complete provider_authority claim, the associated TcxDb implementation file and sole metadata_provider_authority TODO test. Captured the metadata design and accepted external-provider RFD. Source inspection only; no behavioral tests rerun and no source changes.

The claim allows dependency/compiler-authored facts but forbids provider decisions for local resolution, Sage candidate selection, trait proof, alias normalization or checked bodies. The complete typed interface exposes owned definition/path/name/module data, signatures and predicates, associated-item/value facts, conservative inherent-method and trait-impl candidate inventories, ADT properties and procedural macro expansion text. Its return types are owned raw data (vectors, strings, definition identities, RawTy structures and completeness indicators), not Sage CheckedBody, proof outcomes or normalized Sage answers. There is no local resolver, prove, normalize or checked-body operation in this interface.

Candidate inventory is not candidate selection: relevant_trait_impls accepts a fixed trait and optional conservative rigid self head, preserving blanket/unclassifiable headers; inherent_method_candidates requests receiver-bearing declarations by external ADT/name. Likewise associated_type_value returns a named impl's authored type value, not normalization of an arbitrary Sage alias under local assumptions. Procedural macro operations return expansion text to be processed by Sage and do not return typed local-body verdicts. These distinctions are necessary to assess all current interface methods rather than incorrectly rejecting any operation containing the word candidate or source text.

The sole evidence entry is explicitly TODO and contains no assertions. It requires both a typed-interface audit excluding semantic verdict operations and end-to-end evidence that Sage's candidate/solver queries execute after raw fact retrieval. The visible interface supports the first architectural assessment, but the marker and signatures do not establish provider reachability or authority discipline throughout every production call path. Completing those end-to-end trace/semantic tests is the prerequisite for full verification. I preserve that deferral rather than claim that an interface-only read proves every runtime provider obeys the boundary. All claim restrictions and associated entries are accounted for; no concrete interface violation was identified and no edits are requested.
